what_its_for: Ripretinib is a cancer medicine used to treat a type of stomach and intestinal tumor called gastrointestinal stromal tumor (GIST). It is used when other cancer medicines have not worked or are no longer working. It works by blocking certain proteins that help cancer cells grow.
how_to_take: Take ripretinib by mouth once a day, with or without food. Swallow the tablets whole — do not crush, cut, or chew them. Try to take it at the same time every day. If you vomit after taking a dose, do not take another one — just take your next scheduled dose.
dosing: The usual dose is 150 mg (one tablet) taken by mouth once daily. Your doctor may lower your dose or have you take a break from the medicine if you have side effects. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions — do not change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose and it has been LESS than 8 hours since your scheduled time, take it as soon as you remember. If it has been MORE than 8 hours, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at your regular time the next day. Never take two doses in one day to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store ripretinib tablets at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep the tablets in the original container. Keep away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Keep this medicine out of the reach of children and pets. Do not flush unused medicine down the toilet — ask your pharmacist about a medicine take-back program.
what_to_avoid: Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice while taking this medicine, as it can increase the amount of drug in your blood. Avoid St. John's Wort (an herbal supplement), as it can make ripretinib less effective. Tell your doctor or pharmacist about ALL medicines you take, including vitamins and supplements, because many drugs can interact with ripretinib. Avoid prolonged sun exposure and use sunscreen, as this medicine may make your skin more sensitive to sunlight.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you experience: new or worsening high blood pressure, unusual skin changes or sores on your hands or feet (hand-foot skin reaction), chest pain or shortness of breath, fast or irregular heartbeat (this could be a sign of a heart rhythm problem called QT prolongation), muscle or joint pain that is severe, signs of wound healing problems (if you recently had surgery), or if you are pregnant or plan to become pregnant. Also tell your doctor if you plan to have any surgery, as ripretinib may need to be stopped beforehand.
when_it_works: Every patient is different, and it may take several weeks before you or your doctor can tell if ripretinib is working. Your doctor will monitor your progress with regular check-ups and scans. Do not stop taking ripretinib without talking to your doctor first, even if you feel well or do not notice immediate changes.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Ripretinib can harm an unborn baby. Women who could become pregnant must use effective birth control during treatment and for at least 1 week after the last dose. Men with female partners who could become pregnant should also use birth control during treatment and for 1 week after. Do not breastfeed while taking this medicine and for at least 1 week after the last dose. Liver problems: If you have severe liver disease, your doctor may need to adjust your dose. Always tell your doctor about any liver problems before starting this medicine. Children: The safety and effectiveness of ripretinib in children have not been established.
